---
title: "Numbered Code Blocks"
filters:
  - regurgitate
extensions:
  regurgitate:
    number-blocks: true
---

When a document contains many code blocks, referencing specific pieces of code can be challenging. The `number-blocks` option adds sequential labels -- "Code Block 1," "Code Block 2," and so on -- making it to reference code in discussions, reviews, or assignments.

```yaml
extensions:
  regurgitate:
    number-blocks: true
```

## Step 1: Generate Data

```{python}
import random

random.seed(42)
data = [random.gauss(100, 15) for _ in range(50)]
print(f"Generated {len(data)} observations")
print(f"Range: [{min(data):.1f}, {max(data):.1f}]")
```

## Step 2: Clean Data

```{python}
# Remove outliers beyond 2 standard deviations
mean_val = sum(data) / len(data)
std_val = (sum((x - mean_val)**2 for x in data) / len(data)) ** 0.5

lower = mean_val - 2 * std_val
upper = mean_val + 2 * std_val

cleaned = [x for x in data if lower <= x <= upper]
removed = len(data) - len(cleaned)

print(f"Removed {removed} outliers")
print(f"Remaining: {len(cleaned)} observations")
```

## Step 3: Compute Statistics

```{python}
n = len(cleaned)
mean_clean = sum(cleaned) / n
median_clean = sorted(cleaned)[n // 2]
std_clean = (sum((x - mean_clean)**2 for x in cleaned) / (n - 1)) ** 0.5

print("=== Final Statistics ===")
print(f"N:      {n}")
print(f"Mean:   {mean_clean:.2f}")
print(f"Median: {median_clean:.2f}")
print(f"Std:    {std_clean:.2f}")
```

## Step 4: Visualize

```{r}
# Histogram with normal curve overlay
set.seed(42)
cleaned <- rnorm(47, mean = 100, sd = 14)  # Simulated cleaned data

hist(cleaned, 
     freq = FALSE,
     main = "Distribution of Cleaned Data",
     xlab = "Value",
     col = "lightblue",
     breaks = 10)

curve(dnorm(x, mean = mean(cleaned), sd = sd(cleaned)), 
      add = TRUE, col = "darkblue", lwd = 2)
```


## Conclusion

Each block in the appendix below is numbered (Code Block 1, Code Block 2, etc.). This makes it easy to say "see Code Block 2 for the outlier removal logic."
